texts.preamble: Arif Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 November, 2018 1 M.Cr.C. No.48140/18 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh M.Cr.C. No. 48140/18 (Arif Khan Vs. State of M.P.) Gwalior, Dated 30/11/18
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this first application u/S 438 Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail. Petitioner apprehends arrest in connection with offences punishable u/Ss. 270, 272, 273, 420 of IPC r/w 57, 59, 63, 64 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 registered as Crime No.1132/18 at Police Station City Kotwali District Morena. Learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out. Petitioner is apprehending arrest in regard to allegation that he alongwith the other co-accused was preparing adulterated paneer in their factory where ingredients for preparing adulterated paneer have been recovered. The offences alleged against the petitioner are u/S. 270, 272 and 273 of IPC are all bailable though cognizable.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the State has cited decision of the Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre vs. State of Maharashtra and Others 2011 (1) SCC 694 Para 112 to emphasize the relevant consideration which should weigh in the mind of the court while considering the application for anticipatory bail.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the State has cited decision of the Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre vs. State of Maharashtra and Others 2011 (1) SCC 694 Para 112 to emphasize the relevant consideration which should weigh in the mind of the court while considering the application for anticipatory bail.
